original_question: Let f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} be computable by a DNF of size s > 1, and let epsilon in (0,1/2]. Is the Fourier spectrum of f always epsilon-concentrated on some collection F with |F| <= s^{O(log(1/epsilon))}?
target_in_paper: Unnumbered problem "Mansour's Conjecture" in the main problem list (page 4).
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's exact formulation: it has the correct domain and codomain f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, the hypothesis that f is computable by a DNF of size s > 1, the parameter range ε in (0,1/2], and the strong target bound |F| <= s^{O(log(1/ε))} that appears under the heading "Mansour's Conjecture."
missing_details: The quantifiers should be explicit: the statement is for every n, every Boolean function f computable by a size-s DNF, and every ε in (0,1/2].
The Fourier representation should be spelled out to make the question stand-alone: f(x)=Σ_{S⊆[n]} hat f(S) χ_S(x) under the uniform measure on {-1,1}^n.
The collection F should be identified as a set of Fourier characters, equivalently a set of subsets S⊆[n] indexing the Walsh basis.
The meaning of "ε-concentrated" should be made explicit, namely that the squared Fourier mass outside F is at most ε: Σ_{S∉F} hat f(S)^2 <= ε.
The hidden constant in O(log(1/ε)) should be stated as absolute/universal, independent of n, s, f, and ε.
To be fully stand-alone, "DNF of size s" should be glossed as a DNF with s terms.
The paper itself does not define these notations locally; it explicitly refers the reader elsewhere for notation and definitions.
refined_question: For every n >= 1, every Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} computable by a DNF with s > 1 terms, and every ε in (0,1/2], if f has Fourier-Walsh expansion f(x)=Σ_{S⊆[n]} hat f(S) χ_S(x) under the uniform measure on {-1,1}^n, where χ_S(x)=∏_{i∈S} x_i, must there exist a set F⊆2^[n] and an absolute constant C such that Σ_{S∉F} hat f(S)^2 <= ε and |F| <= s^{C log(1/ε)}?
justification: The draft is targeting the exact unnumbered problem labeled "Mansour's Conjecture" on page 4, and it is already almost a verbatim restatement of that item. I only sharpened it by making explicit the standard Fourier-Walsh notation that the paper leaves implicit. This is necessary because the title page says the note assumes external standard notation and definitions. The page-4 remarks also confirm that the intended target is the strong s^{O(log(1/ε))} form, not the weaker nearby variants s^{O_ε(1)} or the consequence from the Fourier Entropy-Influence Conjecture with s^{O(1/ε)}.
